$comment: Refusals the playback compiler raises against constructs a user can author. An entry records who owns the refusal and why it stands; it is not a claim that the refusal is correct. status=live-defect means the document is authorable today and unplayable, and the refusal is a placeholder for work that has not happened; status=intended means the refusal is the answer. Enforced by tools/scripts/negative_capability_check.py.

refusals.reason: MidiContent::create accepts expression lanes, the schema stores them under content.notes.lanes, and the serializer, id remap and note transaction all carry them; the note program has no representation for them, so a clip that authors one does not compile until a renderer chases and emits lane values.

A clip authored with expression lanes stops lowering the moment a SequenceRef trims it, because a lane point before the retained window can still be the value sounding inside it and neither dropping nor carrying it is right; the refusal stands until a chase rule decides what the window inherits.

A nested MIDI leaf with authored groove refuses when SequenceRef trimming changes its source window, because groove displacement can move events across either retained boundary and the compiler has no defined chase, clip or discard rule; the refusal stands until source-window groove inheritance is specified.

set_clip_sequence_ref composes with set_clip_playback_properties, set_track_mixer, set_track_freeze and the take, automation and device-chain surfaces, but flattening has nowhere to fold clip gain and fades, a child fader, a child device chain, takes, freeze, a non-musical anchor, or a trim that cuts a conformed source or a fade, so each of those authored combinations refuses instead of playing wrong.
